title: QoS2 half-handshake retains publish messages and retry ack state
source: MQTT PUBLISH with QoS2 using attacker-controlled packetId and payload, then omitting PUBREL
sink: MqttChannel.qos2MsgCache.put(packetId, wrappedPublishMessage) and TimeAckManager.ackMap via RetryAck.start for PUBREC retries
driver: QoS2 packetId count per connection, payload bytes, number of connections, and missing PUBREL acknowledgements
retention: qos2MsgCache is cleared only by PUBREL or channel close; retry ack state is process-global and static review found no deleteAck on max-retry exhaustion
bound: MQTT packetId space bounds one connection to 65535 in-flight ids and messageMaxSize bounds each payload, but no byte quota or timeout for cached QoS2 publishes was found
impact: plausible default unauthenticated memory exhaustion vector, especially with large QoS2 payloads across many connections. The ackMap leak component should be dynamically confirmed.
static_trigger_shape: CONNECT anonymously, send QoS2 PUBLISH packets with unique packet IDs and payloads, never send PUBREL, keep the connection open or repeat across connections.
scope_notes: No disk storage; marked likely for QoS2 cache, with ackMap stale-entry detail needing probe.
